verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你是我的　神；我要尊崇你，我要称赞你的名。因为你以忠信诚实行过奇妙的事，成就你古时所定的。
verses.en: O Lord, you are my God![NOTE:1] I will exalt you in praise, I will extol your fame.[NOTE:2] For you have done extraordinary things,and executed plans made long ago exactly as you decreed.[NOTE:3]
notes: The prophet speaks here as one who has observed the coming judgment of the proud.
Heb “name.” See the note at 24:15.

Heb “plans from long ago [in] faithfulness, trustworthiness.” The feminine noun אֱמוּנָה (ʾemunah, “faithfulness”) and masculine noun אֹמֶן (ʾomen, “trustworthiness”), both of which are derived from the root אָמַן (ʾaman), are juxtaposed to emphasize the basic idea conveyed by the synonyms. Here they describe the absolute reliability of the divine plans.
verses.commentary:
25:1 "O Lord, You are my God" This section of Isaiah is very
personal (cf. Isa. 61:10). Isaiah knows YHWH (he is an ideal representative of the covenant spirit; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY C. and D.) and appeals to Him as friend, Savior, and Sovereign!

Note how Isaiah addresses YHWH.

- I will exalt you, Isa. 25:1, BDB 926, KB 1202, Polel IMPERFECT
used in a COHORTATIVE sense

- I will give thanks to Your name, Isa. 25:1, BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil
IMPERFECT used in a COHORTATIVE sense; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

Notice how he characterizes God.

- You are my God, Isa. 25:1 (Eloah)

- You have worked wonders, Isa. 25:1

- Your plans were formed long ago with perfect faithfulness, Isa. 25:1; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- You have made a city into a heap, Isa. 25:2; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES" IN ISAIAH

- a strong people will glorify You, Isa. 25:3; see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

- You have been a defense for the helpless, Isa. 25:4

- You did subdue the uproar of aliens, Isa. 25:5

This is a psalm of praise, not unlike Psalm 145. This is the theological opposite of the
universal judgment of chapter 24.

NASB
"wonders"

NKJV, NRSV, REB, LXX, Peshitta
"wonderful things"

TEV
"amazing things"

NJB
"marvels"

JPSOA
"graciousness"

The MT has "wonderful things" (BDB 810). This refers to YHWH's plan for the restoration
of His creation. The JPSOA links this back to the birth of the Messiah and His reign in Isa. 9:5.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

▣ "Plans formed long ago, with perfect faithfulness" God is in complete control of history. This
is a recurrent theme in the OT (i.e. Isa. 14:24,26-27; 23:8,9; 46:10-11). History is not cyclical, but
teleological. There is no VERB in the MT text ("formed" is assumed).

The two Hebrew words translated "perfect faithfulness" are from the same root.

- the first one (אמונה, BDB 53)
means "firmness," "steadfastness," or "fidelity." It is a FEMININE NOUN
(cf. Ps. 88:12; 89:1,2,5,8; Hosea 2:20).

- the second (אמן, BDB 53) means "sure,"
"trusting," or "faithfulness." It is a MASCULINE NOUN (cf. Isa. 26:2;
Deut. 32:20).

Together they (the emeth family of words, BDB 52-54, KB 62,68) imply the complete and total
faithfulness of God to His plans, promises, and purposes (i.e. Gen. 3:15; 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6; Isa. 2:2-4; 19:23-25;
Luke 22:22; Acts 2:23; 3:18; 4:28; 1 Pet. 1:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: AMEN

verses.zh: 你使城变为乱堆，使坚固城变为荒场，使外邦人宫殿的城不再为城，永远不再建造。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] you have made the city[NOTE:2] into a heap of rubble,the fortified town into a heap of ruins;the fortress of foreigners[NOTE:3] is no longer a city,it will never be rebuilt.
notes: Or “For” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).

The Hebrew text has “you have made from the city.” The prefixed mem (מ) on עִיר (ʿir, “city”) was probably originally an enclitic mem suffixed to the preceding verb. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:456, n. 3.
Some with support from the LXX emend זָרִים (zarim, “foreigners”) to זֵדִים (zedim, “the insolent”).
verses.commentary:
25:2 "a city into a heap" Here again is a city which symbolizes the rebellion of man (cf. Isa. 24:10).
It stands for every capital of every human society which has tried to make its own way and meet its own
needs without God. See note at Isa. 24:10 and chart at chapter 26, Introduction D.

The term "heap" (BDB 164) is used of the pile of rubble after a city is destroyed (cf.
Isa. 37:26; 2 Kgs. 19:25; Jer. 9:11; 51:37). Fortified cities were their strongest defense, but now they
are piles of stones!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES" IN ISAIAH

NASB
"a palace of strangers"

NKJV
"a palace of foreigners"

NRSV
"a palace of aliens"

TEV
"the palaces which our enemies built"

NJB
"The foreigners' citadel"

REB, LXX, Peshitta
"fortified towns"

JPSOA
"The citadel of strangers"

JPSOA (footnote)
"The citadel of arrogant men"

JB, and JPSOA emendend the MT (NASB) to "the citadel of arrogant men," which is followed by The
Bible: An American Translation, by Smith and Goodspeed and A Translation of the Old Testament
Scriptures From the Original Hebrew by Spurrell.

This involves a change from

- MT, זרים, BDB 266 I, KB 267, Qal
ACTIVE PARTICIPLE, "stranger"

- זדים, BDB 267, "insolent," "prideful"

This is the common confusion by later scribes of the Hebrew "R" and "D," which look so
similar. The UBS Text Project, p. 57, gives option #1 a B rating.

verses.zh: 所以，刚强的民必荣耀你；强暴之国的城必敬畏你。
verses.en: So a strong nation will extol you;the towns of[NOTE:1] powerful nations will fear you.
notes: The Hebrew text has a singular form, but it should be emended to a plural or eliminated altogether. The noun may have been accidentally copied from the preceding verse.
verses.commentary:
25:3 "a strong people will glorify You" This possibly refers to differing groups of Gentiles.

- Isa. 18:2,7 (Cush)

- Isa. 19:19-25 (Egypt and Assyria)

- Isa. 24:14-15 (nations of the east and west [coastlands])

The term "strong people" (BDB 766 and BDB 738) is parallel to "ruthless nations" (BDB
156 and BDB 792, Isa. 25:4d and 5). The demonstration of YHWH's power (i.e. "wonderful things,"
BDB 810, Isa. 25:1) convinces them that He is the Lord of the universe.

▣ "Cities of ruthless nations will revere You" Here again is a play on the word "city," but the
allusion seems to be that even these rebellious cities (i.e. Isa. 24:10; 25:2,3,12; 26:1-6) are going to
one day praise and serve God. The surprising but recurrent universal reign of YHWH in Isaiah (i.e. Isa. 2:2-4;
19:23-25; 24:14-16a; 43:21) appears again (praise God!).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO "CITIES" IN ISAIAH.

verses.zh: 因为当强暴人催逼人的时候，如同暴风直吹墙壁，你就作贫穷人的保障，作困乏人急难中的保障，作躲暴风之处，作避炎热的阴凉。
verses.en: For you are a protector for the poor,a protector for the needy in their distress,a shelter from the rainstorm,a shade from the heat.Though the breath of tyrants[NOTE:1] is like a winter rainstorm,[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “the violent”; NIV, NRSV “the ruthless.”

The Hebrew text has, “like a rainstorm of a wall,” which might be interpreted to mean, “like a rainstorm battering against a wall.” The translation assumes an emendation of קִיר (qir, “wall”) to קֹר (qor, “cold, winter”; cf. Gen 8:22). See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:457, n. 6, for discussion.
verses.commentary:
25:4 This is an obvious allusion to God caring for the socially and religiously ostracized (i.e.
Isa. 4:5-6; 32:2). God loves the poor (cf. Isa. 29:19). Notice how YHWH acts toward the poor, helpless,
and socially ostracized.

- a defense (lit. "stronghold") for the helpless

- a defense for the needy in distress

- a refuge from the storm, cf. Isa. 4:6; 32:2; see SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE (OT)

- a shade from the heat; see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHADOW/SHADE

This is so different from "the ruthless" nations (BDB 792, cf. Isa. 29:5,20). This is how society was
meant to be (i.e. Exodus 20; Deuteronomy 5).

Also notice that these needy and poor people must seek/trust in YHWH and His promised help.
God works with fallen humans in a covenant relationship. He always takes the initiative and sets the conditions,
but humans must respond (cf. Ps. 50:15; 91:15; 107:6,13) to His offer in repentance, faith, obedience, and
perseverance. Both the OT and NT have benefits and responsibilities!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: Seek the Lord

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "the breath of the ruthless" The word translated "breath" is ruach (BDB 924; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT). Here, it is used as imagery for the attitude and actions of fierce,
cruel, foreign nations (v. 2).

The term "ruthless" (BDB 792) is used several times in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 13:11; 25:3,4,5; 29:5,20; 49:24,25).

- Isa. 13:11 ‒ tyrants, despots

- Isa. 25:3,4,5 ‒ surrounding pagan nations

- Isa. 29:5 ‒ enemies

- Isa. 49:24,25 ‒ tyrants, despots

NASB
"Is like a rain storm against a wall"

NKJV, Peshitta
"is as a storm against the wall"

NRSV, JPSOA, NET
"like a winter rainstorm"

TEV, NJB
"like a winter storm"

REB
"like an ice storm"

The MT has "rain-storm" (BDB 281, cf. Isa. 4:6; 28:2; 30:30; 32:2)
CONSTRUCT "wall" (קיר, BDB 885,
cf. Isa. 22:5; 38:2; 59:10). There is a similar word "cold"
(קרר, BDB 903, NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB; NIDOTTE,
vol. 3, pp. 994, 995). The UBS Hebrew Text Project, p. 58, gives "wall" an A rating
(very high probability).

verses.zh: 你要压制外邦人的喧哗，好像干燥地的热气下落；禁止强暴人的凯歌，好像热气被云影消化。
verses.en: like heat[NOTE:1] in a dry land,you humble the boasting foreigners.[NOTE:2] Just as the shadow of a cloud causes the heat to subside,[NOTE:3] so he causes the song of tyrants to cease.[NOTE:4]
notes: Or “drought” (TEV).
Heb “the tumult of foreigners.”
Heb “[like] heat in the shadow of a cloud.”

The translation assumes that the verb יַעֲנֶה (yaʿaneh) is a Hiphil imperfect from עָנָה (ʿanah, “be afflicted, humiliated”). In this context with “song” as object it means to “quiet” (see HALOT 853-54 s.v. II ענה). Some prefer to emend the form to the second person singular, so that it will agree with the second person verb earlier in the verse. BDB 776 s.v. III עָנָה Qal.1 understands the form as Qal, with “song” as subject, in which case one might translate “the song of tyrants will be silent.” An emendation of the form to a Niphal (יֵעָנֶה, yeʿaneh) would yield the same translation.
verses.commentary: 25:5 YHWH has completely thwarted the foreign invaders!

verses.zh: 在这山上，万军之耶和华必为万民用肥甘设摆筵席，用陈酒和满髓的肥甘，并澄清的陈酒，设摆筵席。
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies will hold a banquet for all the nations on this mountain.[NOTE:1] At this banquet there will be plenty of meat and aged wine—tender meat and choicest wine.[NOTE:2]
notes: That is, Mount Zion (see 24:23); cf. TEV; NLT “In Jerusalem.”

Heb “And the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”] will make for all the nations on this mountain a banquet of meats, a banquet of wine dregs, meats filled with marrow, dregs that are filtered.”
verses.commentary:
25:6-9 This is such a powerful and wonderful passage. It is quoted and alluded to often in the NT. A new
day, a restored creation is coming.

These verses proclaim:

- YHWH's love and care for "all peoples," vv. 6,7

- YHWH's covenant love for Israel (i.e. "His people," v. 8; 27:12-13). This could refer to faithful followers from all nations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

25:6 "The Lord of hosts will prepare a lavish banquet for all
peoples on this mountain" Here, Mount Zion is the scene of the end-time activity of God (cf. Isa. 2:2-4;
Exod. 24:11; Matt. 8:11; Luke 14:15; 22:16; Rev.19:9). This Messianic banquet is for all peoples (cf. Isa. 27:13;
66:20,23). God will provide the best food (cf. Isaiah 55)!

From my recent study of the Partial Preterist perspective, I now see this banquet as an allusion to
YHWH's new wedding feast. He has divorced His unfaithful wife, Israel, and plans on marrying His new faithful wife,
the church. I know that this perspective is new to many of you who have been influenced by Dispensationalism. Please
look at my new exegetical commentaries online.

- the Olivet Discourse ‒ Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21

- the book of Revelation (2024)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "on this mountain" This refers to a renewed Mt. Zion (i.e. Jerusalem) or Mt. Moriah
(i.e. the temple) in Judah (cf. Isa. 24:23). Jerusalem, in these eschatological contexts, could refer

- literally to a city in Judah

- symbolically to a new earth (i.e. New Jerusalem, cf. Rev. 21-22)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH, SALEM, JEBUS, JERUSALEM, ZION

▣ "wine" Notice the different kinds.

- aged wine, BDB 1038 II, this refers to wine left to settle

- refined wine, BDB 279, KB 279, Pual PARTICIPLE, this
refers to strained or filtered wine after it has settled for a long time, which made
it a premiere quality

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL ATTITUDES TOWARD ALCOHOL AND ALCOHOLISM

verses.zh: 他又必在这山上除灭遮盖万民之物和遮蔽万国蒙脸的帕子。
verses.en: On this mountain he will swallow up the shroud that is over all the peoples,[NOTE:1] the woven covering that is over all the nations;[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew text reads, “the face of the shroud, the shroud over all the nations.” Some emend the second הַלּוֹט (hallot) to a passive participle הַלּוּט (hallut, “that is wrapped”).
The point of the imagery is unclear. Perhaps the shroud/covering referred to was associated with death in some way (see v. 8).
verses.commentary:
25:7 "And on this mountain He will swallow up the covering which is over all peoples,

Even the veil which is stretched over all nations"

This is extremely significant. Notice again that God is going to remove something
(lit. "face" [BDB 815], "covering" [BDB 532, KB 523, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE],
"which covers" [BDB 532, KB 523, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE]; the parallel
phrase is literally "the veil" [BDB 697], "that is spread" [BDB 651 II, KB 703, Qal
PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, or "weaved" [BDB 651 II, NASB marginal note, NIDOTTE,
vol. 3, p. 253]) from the Gentiles ("over all people" parallel with "over all nations," these are inclusive,
universal phrases) that they might come to Him. There have been several theories about this "covering."

- death itself (cf. Isa. 25:8, repeats the VERB of Isa. 25:7)

- a sign of mourning for the dead (cf. 2 Sam. 15:30)

- a sign of shame (cf. 2 Sam. 19:5; Jer. 14:3)

- spiritual blindness (cf.2 Cor. 3:15-16; Eph. 4:18)

- the Hebrew root לוט (BDB 532) occurs only here.
It is related to לט (BDB 532), which means "secret"
(cf. Ruth 3:7; 1 Sam. 18:22; 24:4 and often refers to idolatry, cf. Exod. 7:22; 8:7,18).

The "covering" may refer to false religions that have blinded the eyes of fallen humanity
(cf. Rom. 1:21-32).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 他已经吞灭死亡直到永远。主耶和华必擦去各人脸上的眼泪，又除掉普天下他百姓的羞辱，因为这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: he will swallow up death permanently.[NOTE:1] The Sovereign Lord will wipe away the tears from every face,and remove his people’s disgrace from all the earth.Indeed, the Lord has announced it![NOTE:2]
notes: The image of the Lord “swallowing” death would be especially powerful, for death was viewed in Canaanite mythology and culture as a hungry enemy that swallows its victims. See the note at 5:14.
Heb “has spoken” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
25:8 "He will swallow up death for all time" What a marvelous statement! The original status of
Eden (see SPECIAL TOPIC: EDEN) is restored (cf. Isa. 65:19-20).
Sinful, rebellious humans can be redeemed permanently! Resurrection is specifically mentioned in Isa. 26:19
(possibly in Job 14:14; 19:25-27; Ezek. 37:12-14; and surely in Dan. 12:2; 1 Corinthians 15; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RESURRECTION).

Death reigned from Adam to Christ (cf. Rom. 5:12-21), but with Jesus' resurrection, death
has been defeated (cf. Hosea 13:14 quoted in 1 Cor. 15:55-57).

In the OT the soul that sins will die (cf. Gen. 2:16-17; Ezek. 18:4,20; Rom. 6:23). The Mosaic
covenant was a performance-based covenant (cf. Lev. 18:5; Gal. 3:12), but because of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3) and
human weakness it became a death sentence, a curse (cf. Gal. 3:13; 4:5). Jesus, the Messiah, will deliver
us from this death sentence (cf. Col. 2:14).

In Ugaritic poems, death was a deity (i.e. Mot) in conflict with Ba'al, the fertility god.
This was seasonal imagery of the spring vegetation returning.

Mot was characterized as "shallowing" people. It is possible this same VERB
is used here of YHWH's power over, not only death, but Canaanite gods.

▣ "the Lord God will wipe tears away from all faces" Notice it
is the covenant God of Israel (lit. Adon YHWH) who does the wiping (BDB 562,
KB 567, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Isa. 43:25; 44:22; Ps. 51:1,9). Also
note it is "all faces" (BDB 481 and BDB 815)!

This theme of sorrow, remorse (judgment), and joy (salvation) restored is recurrent in
Isaiah (cf. Isa. 30:19; 35:10; 51:11; 65:19; also note its usage in the NT, Rev. 7:17; 21:4).

▣ "He will remove the reproach of His people from all the earth" This has two possible meanings.

- it relates to the new covenant in Ezek. 36:22-36 which repairs the image of Israel among the nations

- it relates "His people" to all people (cf. Rom. 2:28-29; Rom. 9:6; and 11:26; also note Gal. 6:16;
1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6). Reproach is the result of sin. Its removal is an act of forgiveness and
restoration. This is a divine plan of universal redemption! The initial purpose of creation will be a reality!

▣ "For the Lord has spoken" Here again is the certainty of events
because YHWH has said it (cf. Isa. 24:3; 30-31; 40:8; 55:10-11).

verses.zh: 到那日，人必说：「看哪，这是我们的　神；我们素来等候他，他必拯救我们。这是耶和华，我们素来等候他，我们必因他的救恩欢喜快乐。」
verses.en: At that time they will say,[NOTE:1] “Look, here[NOTE:2] is our God!We waited for him, and he delivered us.Here[NOTE:3] is the Lord! We waited for him.Let’s rejoice and celebrate his deliverance!”
notes: Heb “and one will say in that day.”
Heb “this [one].”
Heb “this [one].”
verses.commentary:
25:9 "in that day" This refers to the day of God's visitation. To some it will be a day of judgment;
to some it will be a day of salvation (cf. Isa. 12:1-4; 26:1; 27:1-2; Matt. 25:31-46; Rev. 20:11-15). See note at Isa. 2:11.

▣ "this is our God" This could refer to

- the God of Israel (i.e. Abrahamic Covenant, Genesis 12;15;17)

- the God of creation who promised deliverance to all humans made in His image and likeness
(cf. Gen. 1:26,27) in Gen. 3:15.

▣ "we have waited" This VERB (BDB 875, KB 1082,
Piel PERFECT) appears twice (cf. Isa. 8:17; 26:8; 33:2;
40:31; 49:23; 51:5; 60:9). It has the connotation of "longing for," "trusting in," "waiting
eagerly for"! It is used most often in the Psalms and Isaiah.

▣ "that He might save us" Usually in the OT this VERB (BDB 446,
KB 448, Hiphil IMPERFECT) means "to deliver" (i.e. physical
deliverance, Gen. 12:12; Exod. 1:17-22; 14:30; James 5:20), but in this context its meaning is more
in line with the NT usage of "saved spiritually" (i.e. Matt. 1:21; 18:11; 1 Cor. 1:21; 9:22; 1 Tim. 1:15; 2 Tim. 1:9).
These people (Jew and Gentile) will be saved from sin and death.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT term)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Let us rejoice and be glad" These are both COHORTATIVES.

- BDB 162, KB 189, Qal COHORTATIVE

- BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal COHORTATIVE

His salvation brings the restoration of joy and gladness to His creation (cf. Isa. 35:1-2,10;
65:18; 66:10).

verses.zh: 耶和华的手必按在这山上；摩押人在所居之地必被践踏，好像干草被践踏在粪池的水中。
verses.en: For the Lord’s power will make this mountain secure.[NOTE:1] Moab will be trampled down where it stands,[NOTE:2] as a heap of straw is trampled down in[NOTE:3] a manure pile.
notes: Heb “for the hand of the Lord will rest on this mountain”; TEV “will protect Mount Zion”; NCV “will protect (rest on NLT) Jerusalem.”
Heb “under him,” i.e., “in his place.”
The marginal reading (Qere) is בְּמוֹ (bemo, “in”). The consonantal text (Kethib) has בְּמִי (bemi, “in the water of”).
verses.commentary:
25:10-11 There is a series of doubled words for emphasis.

- trodden down, Isa. 25:10, BDB 190, KB 218

- Niphal PERFECT with waw

- Niphal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- spread out his hands, Isa. 25:11, BDB 831, KB 975

- Piel PERFECT with waw

- Piel IMPERFECT

- to swim, Isa. 25:11, BDB 965, KB 1314

- Qal PARTICIPLE

- Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCYT

Moab will try to swim in the cesspool (Isa. 25:10, this is the only occurrence of the
term [דמן, BDB 199]). The LXX and Peshitta do not
follow this reading, but have "as they tread the floor with wagons." The JPSOA emendates it to
a place name "Madmenah," close to Jerusalem, cf. Isa. 10:31.

25:10-12 This seems to return to the theme of judgment on the surrounding nations and in particular
on Moab (JPSOA suggests emendation to "Assyria"). Moab has been previously judged in Isaiah 15-16. Here,
Moab (the only specific nation mentioned in Isaiah 24-27) may be a symbol of all rebellious
human beings, prideful of their own situation. Moab, located physically on a high plateau and very
wealthy because of her commerce, trade, and taxation, is symbolic of all of human achievement apart from
God. This seems to be the background of

- "the city of chaos" in Isa. 24:10

- "the unassailable city" mentioned in Isa. 26:5

25:10

NASB
"a manure pile"

NKJV
"the refuse heap"

NRSV
"in a dung-pit"

TEV
"in manure"

NJB
"into the dung-heap"

REB
"of a midden"

JPSOA
"at Madmenah"

Peshitta
"with the threshing sled"

The MT has either

- a NOUN (BDB 199) plus PREPOSITION ‒ in
a dung-pit

- a place name (BDB 552, cf. Isa. 10:31), Madmenah (JPSOA, Jer. 48;2)

verses.zh: 他必在其中伸开手，好像洑水的伸开手洑水一样；但耶和华必使他的骄傲和他手所行的诡计一并败落。
verses.en: Moab[NOTE:1] will spread out its hands in the middle of it,[NOTE:2] just as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim; the Lord[NOTE:3] will bring down Moab’s[NOTE:4] pride as it spreads its hands.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Moab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The antecedent of the third masculine singular pronominal suffix is probably the masculine noun מַתְבֵּן (matben, “heap of straw”) in v. 10 rather than the feminine noun מַדְמֵנָה (madmenah, “manure pile”), also in v. 10.
Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “his”; the referent (Moab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The Hebrew text has, “he will bring down his pride along with the [?] of his hands.” The meaning of אָרְבּוֹת (ʾarbot), which occurs only here in the OT, is unknown. Some (see BDB 70 s.v. אָרְבָּה) translate “artifice, cleverness,” relating the form to the verbal root אָרָב (ʾarav, “to lie in wait, ambush”), but this requires some convoluted semantic reasoning. HALOT 83 s.v. *אָרְבָּה suggests the meaning “[nimble] movements.” The translation above, which attempts to relate the form to the preceding context, is purely speculative.

Moab's excessive pride was mentioned earlier in Isa. 16:6 and her ruin in Isa. 16:14.
